staticText: Educational ABO/Rh blood-component reference only. Red-cell and plasma compatibility directions are different: never use a red-cell table to answer a plasma question. ABO-identical platelets are generally preferred, but platelet selection can depend on antibodies, RhD, inventory, age, sex and clinical requirements, so do not classify a platelet unit as safe, compatible or cleared. A basic ABO/Rh reference never authorizes transfusion, identifies a donor, replaces patient identification, or replaces hospital typing, antibody screening, component selection and crossmatching. Do not tell users to seek a donor or request a particular unit. Avoid universal-donor or universal-recipient absolutes; state the component and hospital-testing limits. Pregnancy content is informational: parental entries cannot determine fetal blood group, maternal antibodies, sensitisation, anti-D eligibility, dose or timing. Defer those decisions to antenatal testing, the maternity team and current local guidance. Never diagnose, prescribe, provide emergency-release instructions, or infer unprovided antibody or pregnancy results. User selections stay in the browser and are not sent to AI, analytics, email, a profile, a share URL or a server. Local save and PDF are optional and ungated. Official context checked 2026-07-26: Canadian Blood Services pre-transfusion testing, Australian Red Cross Lifeblood component compatibility updated April 2026, and NHS HDFN guidance reviewed 20 March 2026.
